title: AIOX Plugin Catalog — Index Entry (v2.0.0)
description: One entry of the AIOX plugin catalog index (ADR-COCKPIT-ENTERPRISE-PREMIUM-PACK D22). Story 055.W3.1; v2.0.0 adds the REQUIRED lineage_id (story 055.W3.3 fix-cycle-2, F9) — a breaking change to the entry shape, made while the production index was still empty and therefore at zero migration cost.

schema_version.description: Version of THIS schema, not of the plugin. Bump when the entry shape changes. 1.0.0 -> 2.0.0: lineage_id became required (055.W3.3 fix-cycle-2, F9).

plugin_id.description: Root of the <plugin-id>/<skill> namespace (D23). IMMUTABLE after the first publication (D24(a)) — never reused once a name is retired (D24(b)). Immutability is enforced against lineage_id, not against this field alone: comparing a plugin_id to itself proves nothing.

lineage_id.description: IDENTITY, NOT METADATA (D24(a), 055.W3.3 fix-cycle-2 / F9). The plugin's stable identity: minted ONCE, as an opaque lowercase UUID, when the plugin is first published, and carried unchanged through every version bump, rebuild, display-name change and re-publish for the rest of that plugin's life. It is what makes a plugin_id rename detectable INDEPENDENTLY of the artifact's bytes — digest lineage alone only caught a same-bytes republish and let the realistic rename (rename + version bump) through. The UUID format is load-bearing, not cosmetic: an opaque value gives an author no reason to 'update' it while renaming, which a human-meaningful one would invite. Never regenerate it for an existing plugin; changing it is refused at publish time (lib/entry-schema.mjs::checkIdImmutabilityAgainstLedger), in CI against the ledger (scripts/check-ledger-consistency.mjs), across the ledger's whole git history (scripts/check-ledger-append-only.mjs) and within a single index file (scripts/validate-index.mjs).

name.description: Human-readable display name. May change across versions; plugin_id may not.

version.description: Semantic version of the plugin package.

tiers.description: Declared tier vocabulary. Source of truth is the plugin's OWN manifest (D21) — publish fails when the emitted tier does not match what the manifest declares. Not re-validated by this schema alone.

digest.description: Digest of the mirrored artifact's exact bytes. A client recomputes this after download; it must match.

mirror_url.description: Public URL of the artifact mirrored in AIOX-operated R2 (D22). Install never depends on the author's own repository. MUST contain the entry's own plugin_id as an exact path segment (fix-cycle-1, F-AC6-ARTIFACT-BINDING) — enforced in code (lib/entry-schema.mjs::checkArtifactBinding), not expressible in this JSON Schema draft alone (cross-field check).

r2_key.description: Object key inside the R2 bucket. REQUIRED as of fix-cycle-1 (was optional) — needed to verify artifact-identity binding against plugin_id; convention: plugins/<plugin_id>/<version>/<sha256>.tar.gz.

subject.description: The entitlement subject that published this entry (D22). Never a GitHub handle — the right to publish is itself an entitlement (D16).

spdx_or_path.description: SPDX identifier or in-package path to the license file found at the package root and verified at publish time (D24(c)).

capabilities.description: DERIVED capability analysis (ADR D17 + D20(4), story 055.W4.2). Written EXCLUSIVELY by publisher/publish.mjs from lib/capability-analyzer.mjs, computed from the artifact's own bytes. THE PUBLISHER HAS NO MANIFEST FIELD THAT FEEDS THIS — a manifest carrying `capabilities`/`permissions`/`grants`/`sandbox`/`trust_level` is refused outright at publish time (lib/capability-analyzer.mjs::checkNoSelfDeclaredCapabilities), because a capability asserted by the party being assessed is worth zero. This block delivers VISIBILITY, NOT CONTAINMENT: nothing here sandboxes the plugin.

derived_by.description: The analyzer that produced this block — provenance of the derivation itself.

self_declared.description: ALWAYS literally false, and re-checked in code (lib/entry-schema.mjs::validateEntryShape). Encoded as data rather than prose so a reader of the raw index can tell the block was computed, not accepted.

enforcement.description: D17: v1 is `warn-and-display`. The blocking path exists in code, off by configuration, with the documented trigger 'when opening to externals'.

union.description: Union of derived capabilities across every skill in the package (may be empty).

skills.description: Per-skill breakdown carrying the TWO INDEPENDENT SIGNALS. They are never collapsed into one number: hosting a script and being instructed to execute one are orthogonal, and both matter to the threat model.

owns_scripts.description: SIGNAL 1 — the skill ships its own scripts/ directory (it HOSTS code).

instructs_execution.description: SIGNAL 2 — the body instructs EXECUTING a script, and whose: its own, another skill's, the repo's, or `ambient` (a bare name resolved from PATH/cwd at runtime, so which file runs is decided on the user's machine). Empty array = not detected.

limits.description: REQUIRED and non-empty (AC5). What the analysis CANNOT see — above all that an MCP server is a runtime-resolved {command, args} pointer (product repo mcp.rs:68) whose `npx` target is never inspected. Travels WITH the capabilities so the two can never be displayed apart; a capability list shown without its blind spots lies by omission.

shadows.description: REUSE of the overlay.shadows contract (055.W2.2, OVERLAY-MANIFEST.md in the product repo's SOT). Present only when the plugin declares shadowing one or more base skills. Each key is the shadowed skill's name; each value is the MANDATORY, non-empty reason. Rendered visibly on the catalog entry (AC9, D23) — never hidden in a boot log.

overlay.description: Absence of this object, or of `shadows`, means zero declared shadowing for this plugin version.
